set.body:
Objective:
Close the optional Frame ecosystem phase with an evidence-backed compatibility matrix, documentation, and publication boundaries that preserve independent versioning and a credible future extraction path.

Acceptance:
- Every admitted Parquet, query-engine, and Gale adapter publishes an explicit supported type, expression, nullability, ordering, ownership, and platform matrix.
- A Polars/scala-polars adapter is included only after its stability, released-artifact, JNI resource, typed-expression, Arrow handoff, and semantic-conformance findings are recorded; collaboration is preferred to duplicating a mature backend.
- Adapter differential tests use the local Frame interpreter as semantic reference and independent format/kernel oracles where internal consistency would be insufficient.
- Explain and action receipts distinguish decoding, borrowing, sharing, rechunking, compaction, packing, copying, spill, backend translation, and residual local work.
- Examples show the same Frame program executed locally and through at least one production backend, plus a separate explicit transition through the Gale bridge.
- Failure examples demonstrate unsupported-plan, closed-buffer, schema mismatch, null-policy, and backend-semantic rejection.
- Optional artifacts can be omitted without changing Frame core behavior or API.
- Versioning and release policy state which modules are stable, experimental, JVM-only, Scala.js-capable, ScalaFIM-incubated, or demand-gated.
- Extraction documentation separates the core rename/move from independently versioned adapter migrations and does not pre-claim Typelevel organization hosting.
- Saved benchmark and memory receipts support every performance claim; no general zero-copy, out-of-core, or backend-equivalence language exceeds the evidence.
